title: Adaptive empirical-Bayes credible-set calibration and failure

items.title: Hyperrectangle classes in a Gaussian sequence model
Polished-tail class for a Gaussian sequence
Empirical-Bayes credible-ball procedure in the inverse Gaussian sequence model
items.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $n\ge3$, $p\ge0$, $C\ge1$, $\gamma\in(0,1)$,
an inflation factor $L\ge0$, and a finite $A_n>0$. Let
$(\kappa_i)_{i\ge1}$ be known nonzero real numbers satisfying
$$C^{-2}i^{-2p}\le\kappa_i^2\le C^2i^{-2p}.$$
For a true parameter $\theta_0\in\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$, the observation
sequence is
$$X_i=\kappa_i\theta_{0,i}+n^{-1/2}Z_i,\qquad i\ge1,$$
where $(Z_i)_{i\ge1}$ are independent $N(0,1)$ random variables. The
corresponding sampling law is denoted $P_{\theta_0}^{(n)}$.

For $0<\alpha\le A_n$, let
$$\Pi_\alpha=\bigotimes_{i\ge1}N(0,i^{-1-2\alpha}).$$
Its coordinate posterior rule is the product of
$$N\!\left(\widehat\theta_{n,\alpha,i}(x), v_{n,\alpha,i}\right),\qquad \widehat\theta_{n,\alpha,i}(x)= \frac{n\kappa_i x_i}{i^{1+2\alpha}+n\kappa_i^2},\qquad v_{n,\alpha,i}=\frac{1}{i^{1+2\alpha}+n\kappa_i^2}.$$
For $\alpha>0$, the marginal log likelihood relative to the reference law
$\bigotimes_{i\ge1}N(0,n^{-1})$ is
$$\ell_n(\alpha;x)=-\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \left[ \log\!\left(1+\frac{n\kappa_i^2}{i^{1+2\alpha}}\right) -\frac{n^2\kappa_i^2x_i^2}{i^{1+2\alpha}+n\kappa_i^2} \right].$$
For maximization, use this same source score series at every
$\alpha\in[0,A_n]$, with the sum taken in increasing coordinate order.
Choose a Borel data domain $D_n\subseteq\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}$ such that
the series converges to a finite value for every $x\in D_n$ and every
$\alpha\in[0,A_n]$, and $\alpha\mapsto\ell_n(\alpha;x)$ is upper
semicontinuous there. For each truth under consideration assume
$P_{\theta_0}^{(n)}(D_n)=1$. Also assume a Borel-measurable selector
$x\mapsto\widehat\alpha_n(x)$ on $D_n$ is supplied, with
$\widehat\alpha_n(x)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{0\le\alpha\le A_n}
\ell_n(\alpha;x)$.
These domain, endpoint-score and selector conditions are explicit procedure
hypotheses; no arbitrary score value at $\alpha=0$ is added. At
$\widehat\alpha_n>0$, let $r_{n,\gamma}(\widehat\alpha_n)$ be the
$1-\gamma$ quantile of the centered posterior $\ell^2$ norm and use the
posterior mean given above. Define the empirical-Bayes set by
$$\widehat C_n(L;x)= \begin{cases} \{\theta\in\ell^2: \|\theta-\widehat\theta_{n,\widehat\alpha_n(x)}(x)\|_2 \le Lr_{n,\gamma}(\widehat\alpha_n(x))\},& \widehat\alpha_n(x)>0,\\ \ell^2,&\widehat\alpha_n(x)=0. \end{cases}$$
Use the source convention $r_{n,\gamma}(0)=+\infty$ for the second branch;
no posterior probability on $\ell^2$ is asserted at $\alpha=0$. A separate
local lemma verifies the coordinate posterior and evidence formulas for
$\alpha>0$.

items.title: Posterior and marginal-likelihood formulas for the Gaussian sequence prior
Uniform marginal-score bounds by derivative integration
items.statement:
Use the defined inverse Gaussian sequence procedure with fixed $p,C,L_0,N_0,\rho$ and $0<A=A_n\le\sqrt{\log n}/(4\sqrt{\log(\rho\vee e)})$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Write
$$ r_\alpha=1+2\alpha+2p,\quad s_\alpha=1+2\alpha,\quad N_\alpha=n^{1/r_\alpha},\quad V_\alpha=N_\alpha\log N_\alpha,\quad f_\alpha(i)=\frac{n^2i^{s_\alpha}\log i}{(i^{r_\alpha}+n)^2},\quad S_\alpha=\sum_i f_\alpha(i)\theta_i^2,\quad h_\alpha=S_\alpha/V_\alpha. $$
The likelihood has a continuous derivative $M_n$ on $[0,A]$, with the derivative at zero interpreted from the right. Let $Q_n=M_n-E_\theta M_n$. Uniformly over $\theta\in\Theta_{\rm pt}(L_0,N_0,\rho)$,
$$ E_\theta\sup_{0\le\alpha\le A}\frac{|Q_n(\alpha)|}{V_\alpha(1+h_\alpha)}\le\frac{K\{1+A L_0\rho^{1+2A}\log n\}}{\sqrt{N_A}}\longrightarrow0. $$
For all sufficiently large $n$, all $0\le a\le b\le A$, and every such truth,
$$ h_a\le(4+36L_0\rho^{1+2b})\frac{N_b}{N_a}h_b. $$
For every $\theta\in\ell^2$, the expectation satisfies
$$ \frac{E_\theta M_n(\alpha)}{V_\alpha}\ge\frac1{8C^4}-C^4h_\alpha,\qquad \frac{E_\theta M_n(\alpha)}{V_\alpha}\le3C^4-C^{-4}h_\alpha. $$
Finally, for arbitrary $\theta\in\ell^2$ and every deterministic interval $[0,c]\subseteq[0,A]$ on which $h_\alpha\le H$, where $H$ is fixed, one has
$$ E_\theta\sup_{0\le\alpha\le c}\frac{|Q_n(\alpha)|}{V_\alpha}\le\frac{K_H(1+A\log n)}{\sqrt{N_A}}\longrightarrow0. $$
Constants do not depend on $n,A,\theta$. Fixed finite $A$ is allowed by the eventual cap.

items.title: Marginal-likelihood maximizer bracket on polished tails
items.statement:
Use the inverse Gaussian sequence procedure of
[[def-adaptive-empirical-bayes-gaussian-sequence-procedure]] with fixed
$p\ge0$, $C\ge1$, $A>0$, and $\kappa_i^2\in[C^{-2}i^{-2p},C^2i^{-2p}]$.
Fix $L_0\ge1$, $N_0\ge1$, and $\rho\ge2$. Let
$\theta_0\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pt}}(L_0,N_0,\rho)$ with $\theta_{0,1}=0$.
For $n\ge3$ and $\alpha\in[0,A]$, put
$$ N_{n,\alpha}=n^{1/(1+2\alpha+2p)},\qquad h_n(\alpha;\theta_0)= \frac{1+2\alpha+2p}{N_{n,\alpha}\log n} \sum_{i=1}^{\infty} \frac{n^2 i^{1+2\alpha}(\log i)\theta_{0,i}^2} {(i^{1+2\alpha+2p}+n)^2}. $$
Define
$$ \underline\alpha_n= \inf\{\alpha\in[0,A]:h_n(\alpha;\theta_0)\ge(16C^8)^{-1}\}, \qquad \overline\alpha_n= \sup\{\alpha\in[0,A]:h_n(\alpha;\theta_0)\le8C^8\}, $$
with the source conventions $\inf\varnothing=A$ and $\sup\varnothing=0$.
Then the source bracket result is
$$ \inf_{\theta_0\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pt}}(L_0,N_0,\rho),\,\theta_{0,1}=0} P_{\theta_0}^{(n)} \bigl(\underline\alpha_n\le\widehat\alpha_n\le\overline\alpha_n\bigr) \longrightarrow1. $$
More generally, the same conclusion holds with $A=A_n$ whenever
$$ 0<A_n\le\frac{\sqrt{\log n}}{4\sqrt{\log(\rho\vee e)}} $$
for all sufficiently large $n$. Uniformly in the polished-tail class, for all sufficiently large $n$,
$$ \frac{n^{-2\underline\alpha_n/(1+2\underline\alpha_n+2p)}}{n^{-2\overline\alpha_n/(1+2\overline\alpha_n+2p)}}\le\left[128C^{16}\{4+36L_0\rho^{1+2A_n}\}\right]^{1+2p}. $$
In particular, for fixed $A$ the two rates are uniformly comparable. The lower bracket alone is valid uniformly over arbitrary $\theta_0\in\ell^2$, using the same definition of $\underline\alpha_n$ and the same procedure/domain hypotheses:
$$ \inf_{\theta_0\in\ell^2}P_{\theta_0}^{(n)}(\underline\alpha_n\le\widehat\alpha_n)\longrightarrow1. $$

items.title: Posterior radius, bias and noise comparisons for empirical Bayes
items.statement:
Fix $\gamma\in(0,1)$. In the defined inverse Gaussian procedure, let $\theta=(\theta_i)\in\ell^2(\mathbb N,\mathbb R)$ be the true sequence. For $n\ge3$ and $\alpha\in[0,A_n]$ write $q_\alpha=1+2\alpha+2p$, $N_{n,\alpha}=n^{1/q_\alpha}$, $R_{n,\alpha}=N_{n,\alpha}^{-2\alpha}=N_{n,\alpha}^{1+2p}/n$, and
$$h_n(\alpha;\theta):=\frac{q_\alpha}{N_{n,\alpha}\log n}\sum_{i=1}^{\infty}\frac{n^2i^{1+2\alpha}(\log i)\theta_i^2}{(i^{q_\alpha}+n)^2}.$$
Thus $h_n(\alpha;\theta)$ is exactly the score normalization $S_\alpha/(N_{n,\alpha}\log N_{n,\alpha})$ in [[lem-uniform-empirical-bayes-marginal-score-bound]], since $\log N_{n,\alpha}=(\log n)/q_\alpha$. Put
$$B_i(\alpha)=-\frac{i^{1+2\alpha}\theta_i}{i^{1+2\alpha}+n\kappa_i^2},\qquad W_i(\alpha)=\frac{\sqrt n\kappa_i Z_i}{i^{1+2\alpha}+n\kappa_i^2}.$$
When $\alpha$ is fixed in the proof, abbreviate $q=q_\alpha$, $N=N_{n,\alpha}$, and $R=R_{n,\alpha}$; endpoint subscripts such as $q_b$, $N_a$, and $R_b$ denote the corresponding values.
Let $0\le a\le b\le A_n$, with $N_{n,A_n}\to\infty$ and $A_n/N_{n,A_n}\to0$. Constants below depend only on $p,C,L_0,\rho,\gamma$. For all sufficiently large $n$, (i) $r_{n,\gamma}(b)^2\ge d R_{n,b}$ for $b>0$; (ii) if $\theta_1=0$, $\theta\in\Theta_{pt}(L_0,N_0,\rho)$ and $h_n(b;\theta)\le8C^8$, then $\sup_{a\le\alpha\le b}\|B(\alpha)\|^2\le K(1+L_0\rho^{2q_b})R_{n,b}$; (iii) with probability at least $1-K/N_{n,a}$, $\sup_{a\le\alpha\le b}\|W(\alpha)\|^2\le K R_{n,a}$. Part (iii) also holds at $a=0$. At $b=0$ the procedure gives the whole parameter space whenever the selector lies in $[a,b]$.

items.title: Conservative coverage of adaptive empirical-Bayes credible balls on polished tails
items.statement:
Use the Gaussian sequence procedure of
[[def-adaptive-empirical-bayes-gaussian-sequence-procedure]] with fixed
$p\ge0$, $C\ge1$, $A>0$, and
$C^{-2}i^{-2p}\le\kappa_i^2\le C^2i^{-2p}$. Fix $L_0\ge1$, $N_0\ge1$,
$\rho\ge2$, and $\gamma\in(0,1)$. Assume that
$\theta_0\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pt}}(L_0,N_0,\rho)$ and
$\theta_{0,1}=0$. Then there is a finite inflation constant $L>0$,
depending only on the fixed model and class parameters, such that
$$ \inf_{\substack{\theta_0\in\Theta_{\mathrm{pt}}(L_0,N_0,\rho)\\ \theta_{0,1}=0}} P_{\theta_0}^{(n)}\{\theta_0\in\widehat C_n(L)\} \longrightarrow1. $$
This is conservative frequentist coverage tending to one, not exact
asymptotic coverage $1-\gamma$. The source also allows a growing
$A=A_n$ provided
$$ A_n\le \frac{\sqrt{\log n}}{4\sqrt{\log(\rho\vee e)}}. $$
In that case a slowly varying inflation sequence is required; the source
allows $L_n\lesssim(3\rho^{3(1+2p)})^{A_n}$.

items.title: Sparse-gap truth causes empirical-Bayes credible-set undercoverage
items.statement:
The adaptive empirical-Bayes credible balls have nonvanishing frequentist
coverage uniformly over every truth in a hyperrectangle $\Theta_\beta(M)$.

**Explicit sparse-gap construction.**

Use [[def-adaptive-empirical-bayes-gaussian-sequence-procedure]], assume AC,
and fix $\beta>0$, $p\ge0$, $C\ge1$, $\gamma\in(0,1)$ and a finite
$A>\beta$. Run the procedure with the fixed cap $A_n=A$ and
$C^{-2}i^{-2p}\le\kappa_i^2\le C^2i^{-2p}$. Choose
$0<M\le(1984C^8)^{-1}$. Put $s=1+2\beta+2p$, $\rho_j=2^j$,
$n_1=2$, and
$$ n_{j+1}=\left\lceil(2\rho_{j+1}^2)^s n_j\right\rceil,\qquad N_j=n_j^{1/s}. $$
Define the fixed nonnegative truth by
$$ \theta_{0,i}^2=\begin{cases}0,&N_j/\rho_j<i\le N_j\text{ for some }j,\\0,&2N_j<i\le\rho_jN_j\text{ for some }j,\\Mi^{-1-2\beta},&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases} $$
Then $\theta_{0,1}=0$ and $\theta_0\in\Theta_\beta(M)$. For every
deterministic nonnegative inflation sequence satisfying
$$ L_{n_j}\le K_L\sqrt M\,\rho_j^{(1+2p)/(8+8\beta+8p)} $$
eventually for some finite $K_L$, one has
$$ P_{\theta_0}^{(n_j)}\{\theta_0\in\widehat C_{n_j}(L_{n_j})\}\longrightarrow0. $$
The finitely many indices with $n_j<3$ are irrelevant. In particular,
for every $\beta>0$ this gives a counterexample for any fixed cap
$A>\beta$, including constant inflation factors.

title: Adaptive empirical-Bayes credible-set calibration and failure — Examples

items.title: A power-law truth lies in the polished-tail class
items.statement:
Fix $\beta>0$, $M>0$, and $\rho\ge2$. Set
$\theta_{0,1}=0$ and
$\theta_{0,i}=\sqrt M\,i^{-1/2-\beta}$ for $i\ge2$. Let $N_0=2$ and
$L_0=(2\beta+1)/(1-\rho^{-2\beta})$. Then
$\theta_0\in\Theta_\beta(M)\cap
\Theta_{\mathrm{pt}}(L_0,N_0,\rho)$. Consequently, under the hypotheses of
[[thm-adaptive-empirical-bayes-credible-ball-conservative-coverage-on-polished-tails]],
an admissible sufficiently large inflation gives conservative frequentist
coverage tending to one for this truth.

items.title: A sparse-gap truth lies in a hyperrectangle but is undercovered
items.statement:
Assume AC. Fix $\beta>0$, $p\ge0$, $C\ge1$, $\gamma\in(0,1)$,
and a finite $A>\beta$. Run the Gaussian sequence procedure in the cited
counterexample with cap $A_n=A$ and take $0<M\le(1984C^8)^{-1}$. Put $s=1+2\beta+2p$,
$\rho_j=2^j$, $n_1=2$, and recursively let
$n_{j+1}=\lceil(2\rho_{j+1}^2)^s n_j\rceil$. Put $N_j=n_j^{1/s}$.
Then $1<N_1<\rho_1$ and
$n_{j+1}\ge(2\rho_{j+1}^2)^s n_j$. Define $\theta_{0,i}\ge0$ by
$$ \theta_{0,i}^2=\begin{cases}0,&N_j/\rho_j<i\le N_j\text{ for some }j,\\0,&2N_j<i\le\rho_jN_j\text{ for some }j,\\Mi^{-1-2\beta},&\text{otherwise}.\end{cases} $$
The verification below proves $\theta_{0,1}=0$ and
$\theta_0\in\Theta_\beta(M)$. For every deterministic nonnegative inflation sequence satisfying
$L_{n_j}\lesssim\sqrt M\,\rho_j^{(1+2p)/(8+8\beta+8p)}$, coverage of
this fixed truth tends to zero along $n_j$, by
[[cex-sparse-gap-truth-causes-empirical-bayes-credible-set-undercoverage]].
